why: Every learning mechanism was inventing its own update shape: the bounded weight delta existed for mode biases, graph edges had none, n-gram counts had none, and replays had none. A shared typed object is what lets XCFE audit any proposal without knowing which Micronaut produced it. The invariant that makes continuous learning safe is one line: **every fold is accounted for, and only admitted deltas mutate knowledge.**

contract_object.name: LearningDeltaRecord
contract_object.note: the micronaut bounded weight update (micronaut::LearningDelta) is the narrow special case of this record with substrate = mode_bias

fields.target_ref: the exact target inside that substrate (a field ref, an edge source→target, an n-gram key, a mode id)
fields.magnitude: the proposed change, in the substrate's own units
fields.bounds: the declared [lower, upper] the resulting value must respect
fields.confidence: the proposer's confidence in [0, 1]; low confidence defers rather than decides
fields.fold_digest: the invariant of the fold that produced it (so the update names its evidence)
fields.evidence_refs: the supports, including external retrieval references
fields.credit_cause_ref: the specific element the credit or blame attaches to

outcomes.ADMITTED: verified, authorized and applied to the persistent state
outcomes.DEFERRED: evidence retained; confidence or permission insufficient, nothing written
outcomes.REJECTED: violates an invariant or fails verification, nothing written, cause recorded
outcomes.NO_CHANGE: the cycle completed without a justified weight change
outcomes.law: every fold produces exactly one learning artifact with one of these outcomes; DEFERRED and NO_CHANGE are first-class results, not failures

phase_authority.law: phases govern authority over the learning operation, not the modality it may encounter
consequences: Yax may discover a graph relationship and propose a graph_edge delta
Sek may invoke a vector learner and propose a vector_field delta
Ch'en may reject an n-gram proposal
a commit proposed outside Xul is refused, and verification outside Ch'en is refused

commit.law: M_{t+1} = M_t (+) Commit_XCFE(Verify_Ch'en(Delta_t)), where (+) is a versioned authorized update and not necessarily a weight addition
commit.atomicity: a commit is all-or-nothing across every substrate: if one delta in the set is refused, nothing is written, so a crash or a rejection cannot leave GramStore, vector fields and GML topology partially updated
commit.idempotence: a delta already committed for the same fold digest is not applied twice; the second attempt reports NO_CHANGE with a duplicate reason
commit.receipt: each commit returns a receipt naming the committed set, the refused set, the deferred set and a digest over them
commit.corpus_prior: no delta mutates the frozen corpus prior; vector deltas apply to W_learned and W_effective = W_corpus * W_learned stays a separate product

credit_assignment.law: rejection condemns the element named by credit_cause_ref, not every element that participated
credit_assignment.why: a rejected candidate does not prove that each edge involved was wrong; blame has to identify the actual cause of failure or the system learns the wrong lesson

invariants.LD1: every delta names exactly one substrate and one target_ref; an unknown substrate or an empty target is refused
invariants.LD2: the outcome vocabulary is ADMITTED, DEFERRED, REJECTED, NO_CHANGE; every fold yields exactly one learning artifact with exactly one outcome per proposed delta, so every fold is accounted for
invariants.LD3: only ADMITTED mutates knowledge; DEFERRED, REJECTED and NO_CHANGE write nothing to any substrate
invariants.LD4: proposal is authorized in Pop, Wo, Yax and Sek; verification only in Ch'en; commit only in Xul — and modality is never phase-locked, only authority is
invariants.LD5: provenance is mandatory: a delta with no provenance_ref or no fold_digest is REJECTED with its reason, never silently dropped
invariants.LD6: a delta is bounded: a resulting value outside the declared bounds is REJECTED rather than clamped without a record
invariants.LD7: a REJECTED delta names the specific cause in credit_cause_ref, and rejection of one delta never condemns the other elements of the same fold
invariants.LD8: confidence below the declared threshold produces DEFERRED with the evidence retained; only invariant failure produces REJECTED
invariants.LD9: commit is idempotent: the same (substrate, target_ref, fold_digest) committed twice is applied once, and the replay reports NO_CHANGE with a duplicate reason
invariants.LD10: commit is atomic: a set containing one refused delta writes nothing anywhere
invariants.LD11: no delta mutates the frozen corpus prior; learned state and corpus evidence stay separate
invariants.LD12: a fold has two distinct outputs — a response artifact and a learning artifact — and closing with zero admitted deltas is a valid, fully accounted-for result
